title: OpenAI CEO Puts Cold Water on AI: AI Won't Bring a Four-Day Workweek, Humans Will Be Busier in the Era of Super Intelligence

content_html:
Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI, recently made a surprising statement in a public interview—AI will not bring the golden era of working four days a week as many people expect. For a long time, every technological revolution has been accompanied by the assumption that technological progress would reduce working hours and provide more leisure time. However, Altman pointed out that this idealized vision has never been widely realized over the decades, and AI will be no different.

Altman admitted that, looking at historical trends, modern people do have more free time for leisure compared to workers hundreds of years ago, and the overall quality of life has reached heights unimaginable in the past. However, the widespread adoption of AI technology will rapidly boost the overall productivity of society. At the same time, the expectations individuals have for themselves will also rise quickly, and there will be no widespread trend of relaxing and reducing workloads.

Unending relative competition drives everyone to be busier rather than more relaxed

In Altman's view, human society's overall needs will never remain at the current level. After productivity increases, people will constantly come up with new things to accomplish, creating new services and products for each other, which in turn give rise to entirely new demands that did not exist before. The operation of society is more like an unending relative competition—everyone is very concerned about where they stand compared to others around them. This drive continuously pushes the economy forward and will not stop because of the arrival of AI.

He even gave a counterintuitive prediction: once the era of super intelligence is fully implemented, everyone's actual condition will be much busier than expected, complaining about how much time work takes, but secretly enjoying it. The reality seems to support this judgment—currently, many tech company executives around the world are actually reinforcing strict rules requiring employees to work five days a week in the office, and some regions are even subtly promoting a 996 overtime culture. The originally hoped-for ideal of a four-day workweek seems to be getting further away from the public.

content_html_zh:
OpenAI首席执行官萨姆·奥尔特曼（Sam Altman）最近在公开采访中发表了令人惊讶的言论——AI不会像许多人期望的那样带来每周工作四天的黄金时代。 长期以来，每次技术革命都伴随着这样的假设：技术进步将减少工作时间并提供更多休闲时间。 不过，奥特曼指出，这种理想化的愿景几十年来从未得到广泛实现，人工智能也不例外。

奥特曼坦言，从历史趋势来看，现代人相比数百年前的劳动者确实拥有更多的空闲时间休闲，整体生活质量达到了过去难以想象的高度。 然而，人工智能技术的广泛采用将迅速提升社会整体生产力。 与此同时，个人对自己的期望也会快速上升，不会出现普遍的放松和减少工作量的趋势。

无休止的相对竞争促使每个人变得更加忙碌而不是更加放松

在奥特曼看来，人类社会的整体需求永远不会停留在目前的水平。 生产力提高后，人们会不断地想出新的事情来完成，为彼此创造新的服务和产品，进而产生以前不存在的全新需求。 社会的运作更像是一场无休止的相对竞争——每个人都非常关心自己与周围其他人相比的地位。 这种动力不断推动经济前进，不会因为人工智能的到来而停止。

他甚至给出了一个反直觉的预测：一旦超级智能时代全面实现，每个人的实际状况都会比预想的忙碌得多，抱怨工作花费了多少时间，却暗自享受。 现实似乎也支持了这个判断——目前，全球许多科技公司高管实际上都在强化严格的规定，要求员工每周在办公室工作五天，有些地区甚至在潜移默化地推行996加班文化。 原本希望的每周工作四天的理想似乎离公众越来越远。
